terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; from something, ab or ex and the ablative
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.78: sīc mē servāvit Apollō
Caes. BG 2.15 (Lewis & Short): Caesar sēsē eōs cōnservātūrum dīxit

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō); with ex or ab and the ablative, or the dative
evidence: Caes. BG 1.53 (Lewis & Short): ē manibus hostium
Vulg. Mt. 8.25: Domine, salvā nōs: perīmus.
terms.comment: Late Latin (Lewis & Short). The Vulgate also says salvum facere: Domine, salvum mē fac (Mt. 14.30).
Lewis & Short: late Latin; the classical word is servātor.

phrases.latin: Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.
phrases.english: The gods are looking after me: all is well.
Lord, save us: we are perishing.

sources: Lewis & Short: servo · Lewis & Short: conservo · Lewis & Short: eripio · Lewis & Short: salvo · Lewis & Short: salvator
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 262, 370, 374, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. save (eccl.).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-plautus, loci-vulgata), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
